release_review.summary: Redeven v0.10.0 consumes published Floret v3.2.32 through one composition-root runtime.Host, immutable runtime.Agent values, transactionally indexed canonical thread inventory with batch latest turns, native narrow capability views, single-snapshot atomic thread bootstrap, authoritative projections, and receipt-bound Floret-assigned ThreadID, TurnID, and RunID values while retaining only product-owned settings, resources, unadmitted queue state, authorization evidence, and durable cross-store coordination.
release_review.same_window_rationale: The Runtime Service wire protocol remains redeven-runtime-v1. The project has not been released or distributed, so this change intentionally establishes ai_threadstore_product_v1 version 1 as the sole first-release product baseline and removes every discarded pre-release migration, parser, and fallback. Future versions must migrate this baseline automatically under the same database kind.
checked_surfaces: Redeven consumes github.com/floegence/floret/v3 v3.2.32 only from the published module with exact checksums, GOWORK=off verification, and no replace, go.work, sibling source path, copied contract, internal import, or Floret schema access

Provider attempts retain one logical request identity and monotonic epoch; Floret fences stale stream and canonical projection facts, while Flower clears only the matching in-memory assistant draft on a newer activation and never checkpoints attempt state

Thread inventory pagination, canonical path, latest turn, authority, and revision are read from Floret's transactionally derived inventory record without per-thread bootstrap or complete session-tree domain decoding; Redeven preserves product order, stops after all requested roots are found, and fails closed when a product root is absent

Thread bootstrap projects thread, turn, approval, todo, context, pending-tool, and SubAgent reads from one canonical Floret backend snapshot and exact revision, uses the same process-local execution registry as ordinary reads so an admitted or executing turn remains running, and preserves gap-free subscription handoff without repeated complete-domain decoding or a downstream cache

Floret v3.2.32 reuses a validated decoded domain only while the exact durable envelope bytes in the current backend snapshot remain unchanged; changed, corrupt, drifted, and future state still follows strict decoding and fail-closed validation, while Redeven remains outside the upstream schema and cache boundary

The single-snapshot bootstrap preserves ErrThreadDeleted for tombstoned identities and ErrThreadNotFound only for absent identities, so product settings that outlive canonical deletion continue to fail closed with the established public classification

Every failed Floret engine result carries an explicit provider, tool-dispatch, storage, cancellation, or engine-contract origin, so AgentHarness persists the original failure instead of replacing it with a secondary missing-classification error

Interrupted tool batches that persist a canceled terminal result without a later run-end marker close any requested approval as canceled, so canonical root inventory and latest-turn projection remain readable before startup recovery runs

Floret v3.2.32 shares one live projection recorder across the Host harness and execution event paths, so approval lifecycle details advance the existing tool item's waiting or pending state without replacing its host-authored label, renderer, description, or payload; exact thread, turn, run, and tool identity prevents cross-turn reuse, and approval-only history retains a neutral fallback presentation

Floret v3.2.32 carries detached tool-authored presentation through effect dispatch and host authorization into every new canonical approval entry, excludes presentation from approval request fingerprints and replay identity, and recovers missing presentation in earlier v3 journals from the matching durable tool call in the same thread and turn without rewriting schema v4 state

Parseable schema-invalid tool calls may retain only sanitized host presentation through Floret v3.2.32 InvalidActivity; they still fail before resources, permission, approval, effects, and handlers, while malformed JSON receives no presentation fallback

Flower bootstrap suppresses a stale in-memory approval action only when a validated canonical terminal Activity item has the exact same RunID and tool-call ID; identity mismatch fails closed, a removed current action clears the sampled queue instead of promoting stale state, and no Floret-owned record is mutated

The composition-root runtime.Host owns Floret storage and issues native ThreadReader, ThreadLifecycle, TurnExecutor, ThreadCompactor, and SubAgentManager capabilities plus narrow create, inventory, and recovery coordinators; direct-child recovery binds through the parent ThreadReader.Child capability, and execution paths do not retain runtime.Host, storage.Backend, aggregate recovery authority, or wrappers for removed broad Thread methods

Published Floret v3.2.32 is the single persistent source of truth for admitted conversation entries, provider-owned thread titles, ThreadID, TurnID, RunID, turn and run lifecycle, projections, approvals, todos, tool state, SubAgent hierarchy, artifacts, and opaque provider state

Floret v3.2.32 preserves running lifecycle projection across atomic ThreadReader.Bootstrap, the initial durable admission-to-execution-registration handoff, and later durable heartbeat renewal-to-registry intervals. The admission proof is bound to the exact thread and turn, heartbeat successors stay within one monotonic authority lineage, and expired, replaced, restarted, claimed, or identity-drifted authority remains fail closed

Approval-gated effect callbacks inherit the active turn's renewable lease binding. Approval, provider, effect, and terminal writes accept only monotonic heartbeat successors within the same thread, turn, owner, generation, and acquisition authority; a stale final heartbeat is absorbed only after durable terminal settlement and local lease cleanup, while identity drift remains fail closed

Canceling a turn while its effect waits for approval uses the current Floret v3.2.32 renewed lease proof to atomically cancel the approval batch and canonical turn, keeps the admission replayable, and does not execute the pending tool or leave startup recovery to reinterpret a normal stop as failure

Create and fork requests use stable browser client_request_id values and durable Redeven operation receipts; Floret alone assigns canonical thread identities, and retries replay the same LogicalRequestID and verify the same canonical result before product materialization

Queued admission persists only a stable queue_id before admission; turn_id and run_id remain empty until a validated Floret TurnAdmissionReceipt binds the Floret-assigned identities in the same transaction as permission proof and product settlement; execution then receives only that receipt and process-local ExecutionContext, while committed-user events remain observation only and cannot bind admission

Unknown admission outcomes retain the draft and stable client_request_id for exact retry, while definite pre-admission failures release the staging scope; neither path generates a replacement canonical identity or reconstructs an admitted user message

Initial Flower presentation maps one atomic Floret ThreadReader.Bootstrap revision, canonical Activity reads use ReadAuthoritativeProjection, and timeline, attachment, reference, approval, todo, terminal settlement, and SubAgent presentation consume validated Floret v3 public snapshots and typed payloads with parent-scoped SubAgent validation; unavailable canonical projections remain the explicit turn_projection_unavailable state, without metadata parsing, legacy DTOs, shadow lifecycle storage, or display synthesis

The Redeven-owned AI product database kind is ai_threadstore_product_v1 and its first-release schema version is 1. Fresh stores initialize directly at version 1 and current stores open only after a read-only, existing-only complete reviewed-schema preflight

Existing ai_threadstore_product_v2 files, discarded pre-release versions, unknown kinds, future versions, malformed metadata, and schema drift are rejected without changing the main database bytes, metadata, timestamps, or SQLite sidecar state

The v1 reset is a one-time user-approved pre-launch exception. After this baseline is merged and released or distributed, every v2 and later product schema must retain the same kind and provide contiguous atomic n-to-n+1 automatic migrations with reviewed source and target snapshots

Redeven opens the current Floret v3.2.32 storage source directly through the published runtime API. Floret automatically migrates released domain schema v2 through v3 to current v4 before Host availability, commits the canonical domain and derived root inventory atomically, verifies exact agreement at current startup, and projects supported interrupted approval history into coherent terminal state; Redeven does not inspect or migrate Floret-owned data. Removed PreflightV2Migration, ApplyV2Migration, ErrMigrationRequired, storage.MigrateV2, compatibility parsers, and substitute migration paths cannot be called

Thread deletion persists an immutable user-intent and upload cleanup snapshot, deletes canonical Floret state first, and preserves product data unless only Floret's exact tombstone replay returns success; a missing canonical thread without that tombstone fails terminally and preserves product data

Provider adapters consume Floret v3 public contracts, map typed messages directly to provider wire shapes, and fail closed on invalid roles, ordering, tool arguments, results, provider state, attachment membership, permission proof, or public projection data

Runtime Service protocol_version remains redeven-runtime-v1, compatibility_epoch remains 8, and both minimum product versions remain v0.10.0 because this dependency and storage reset does not add a second Runtime Service wire shape
